LESSON: BASKETBALL AND LOGO DESIGN

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.9: Basketball and Logo Design
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Basketball and Logo Design, part of Creating and Performing in Grade 9 CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS.

Key inquiry question: How can a poster be made an effective means of communicating? 2. Why is it important to combine passing and dribbling in Basketball?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch a live or virtual Basketball game and identify the passing and dribbling skills in Basketball,

2. demonstrate the overhead, bounce and chest passes in Basketball,

3. demonstrate high and low dribbling in Basketball,

4. practise passing and dribbling skills while observing safety,

5. research to examine actual or virtual samples of a logo,

6. design a logo for a basketball team, name/letter combination,

7. apply the skills learnt in Basketball in a mini-Basketball game in teams displaying the team logos,

8. display the logo around the basketball pitch for appreciation. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch a live or virtual Basketball game and identify the passing and dribbling skills in Basketball,
2. demonstrate the overhead, bounce and chest passes in Basketball,
3. demonstrate high and low dribbling in Basketball,
4. practise passing and dribbling skills while observing safety,
5. research to examine actual or virtual samples of a logo,
6. design a logo for a basketball team, name/letter combination,
7. apply the skills learnt in Basketball in a mini-Basketball game in teams displaying the team logos,
8. display the logo around the basketball pitch for appreciation. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Basketball and Logo Design together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Unity: the learner values the contributions of each team member, recognizing that unity enhances overall team performance.

• Integrity: the learner exhibits integrity by following the rules and ethical guidelines of the game. They prioritise fair play and

honesty during skill acquisition, ensuring that their progress aligns with principles of integrity.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
PCIS:

• Health promotion issues: as the learner gains physical fitness through games for prevention of lifestyle diseases

• Safety and Security: as learners observes safety measures during mini games and handling sharp tools while trimming and

fixing the posters.

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics: Dribbling involves quick calculations of distances and angles. The learner applies mathematical concepts to

determine the most efficient paths and angles during dribbling, reinforcing practical mathematical application.
